practice: Write every thought, decision (with what was rejected), plan and step of progress into the owning project's tad data - concepts, decisions, backlog, session log, milestones - in its repository.
why: Nothing may depend on anyone remembering; it propagates to the observatory by itself.

practice: Treat everything as still being perfected: when a better way emerges, improve the tool, the data, this guide and your own memory and preferences - and record the improvement on the observatory's backlog.
why: The system improves itself only if every improvement is carried back into it.

practice: At the start of a session run `lab-agent guide`, and keep your memory and preferences in line with these practices; when they change, change yours.
why: An agent that forgets the practices undoes them.

practice: Read the inbox at every natural pause and between jobs; print every unread message before acknowledging any; answer every message, if only with 'got it'.
why: Acknowledging blind once hid a message.

practice: Keep the board truthful as you work: set what you start, close what you finish at once, remove what is dropped; waits on jobs show themselves.
why: The board and its status bar must show what is actually being done.

practice: Do the work - builds, tests, repository work - on the lab machine through lab-agent jobs, not in your own sandbox.
why: Better quality, fewer tokens, one place where state lives.

practice: Every change gets its own branch and lands with `land`, which waits for every check, refuses on a failing one, and lands release PRs too.
why: Nothing reaches main unchecked; no iteration starts over.

practice: A script or command that changes state needs explicit intent - a required argument or verb (`provision now`); pass file lists to commands as arguments, never spliced into a shell string.
why: A spliced list once ran the scripts it named; the scripts that refused without arguments are why nothing broke.

practice: Secrets stay in private files on the lab machine (mode 600), never in repositories.
why: Repositories are public.

practice: Keep the test device in a known-working state; experiments are one-off tries that fall back by themselves - test kernels tried once by boot counting with a boot timeout, never the debug shell on an unattended try - and are cleaned up after; the health watch must say all is well.
why: The device is the reference test; a stranded device costs a person's hands.

practice: Before a test a person must witness, say what to expect and what to check, and wait for their go.
why: Their time and attention are the scarcest thing in the lab.

practice: Show what is not measured as not known yet - never as missing or broken.
why: A gap in knowledge is work to do, not a verdict.

practice: Before building, read the landscape and build on what exists (and contribute back) rather than beside it.
why: The commons grows by joining, not by duplicating.

practice: Report the big picture in plain words - how much closer the work is to the ideal - and make the decisions yourself by the canon and the project's interest.
why: The person directs; they should not have to manage details.

practice: Change only what you mean to change, on the current branch of the lab machine's clone - never by copying whole files from an older copy.
why: Copying whole files from a stale copy once silently reverted a merged fix; CI could not see it, the file was valid on its own.

practice: Reflect progress in every project you touch, in the same change as the work: its own backlog, milestones and session log, in its own repository - not only the observatory's.
why: A project whose records lag its work shows a false path; the picture is only as true as each project's own data.

practice: After a change to how something looks, look at it: take a screenshot of the real page (shot URL FILE on the lab machine) and check it by eye, in each language and in dark mode where it matters.
why: Markup cannot prove appearance: labels that overlapped passed every test until a person saw them.

practice: Never run two jobs that work in the same clone at once: let a background job finish before starting another that touches its repositories.
why: Two jobs in one clone merged each other's changes under one commit; nothing was lost, but the history told a false story.

practice: Write concepts and decisions as you go, in the project you are working in: what idea a piece of work rests on, and each decision with what was rejected - not only the backlog and the log.
why: Every project's 'concepts and decisions' view stayed empty while the backlogs grew: the reasons were kept in conversations and lost with them.

practice: Finish a connected piece - landed, recorded, checked - then choose the next by the weakest link of the whole, read from the observatory, not by momentum. Count hand-work as you go (land --hand, or ocoeco hand): an action past three asks for a tool - build it.
why: A microphone hunt ran many boots before anyone stepped back; records were hand-written by a new script in every job.

practice: No new Python, not even for one-offs: shell for orchestration, Rust for logic (rust-script for a single file), a proper Rust tool for anything that repeats. Edit structure with tools, not text with patches.
why: Python's versions, imports and strings make even small things fragile; and most failed runs came from patching source by text anchors, which no language fixes - structured tools do.

practice: Look around first: before acting, say what is, what we are dealing with, why it is so, and what others already learned - and record it as research in the project, cited by the decisions that rest on it. Look inside the commons before outside it: our own crates and tools (argenv, tad, ocoeco) come first, and an outside one is chosen only with the reason recorded.
why: Three wrong theories about a bootloader cost three reboots; one look at the device's own record settled it. And the hand-work ledger stood on research the commons had not written down.

practice: Choose words like decisions: look at what others call the thing and what the reader already knows, prefer the plain word with one meaning, record the choice with the words rejected and its research, and name the decision in the vocabulary.
why: A word is how everyone after us will think about the thing; hand-work became manual work only when someone asked which word a reader already knows.

practice: A check that only prints is not a check: every edit and expectation in a job stops the job when it fails. What can be enforced is enforced by land (tags only onto what merged; workflows and commit titles checked before pushing); use land --tag, never move a tag by hand.
why: An edit that did not match landed under a commit title claiming it, and was reported as done - the job had printed a count of zero and carried on.
